sections.overview: Syndemis musculana is a tortrix moth recorded across Europe, including Britain and Ireland.
sections.identification: Its grey forewings vary from pale to brownish grey and may have faint or indistinct markings; wingspan is 15–22 mm.
sections.habitat: In Britain and Ireland it occurs in varied settings, including woodland, moorland and mountain habitats.
sections.diet: The caterpillars are highly polyphagous and feed on many plants; British records include bramble, birch and oak.
sections.behavior: Adults fly in late afternoon and evening in May and June in Britain, and can come to light after dusk.
sections.reproduction: Larvae feed from leaves spun or folded around them, then overwinter fully grown before pupating in spring.
sections.ecology: Its broad larval diet lets it use trees, shrubs, herbs and grasses rather than a single host plant.
sections.conservation: A French regional records portal says the species has not been assessed in a regional red list; this is not a global status assessment.
